change: Train b292 broad native PGO after excluding exact pre-MMU inlined profile owners fdt_raw, log and ax_alloc in generate/use; require counter-free someboot disassembly before board
hypothesis: The run880 silent startup is due to pre-MMU atomic profile counters from fdt_raw/log/allocator code inlined into someboot; excluding these owners while keeping post-MMU runtime crates profiled will permit boot and preserve broader coverage than four-crate PGO
difference: Exclusions are derived from exact run880 ELF counter record owners, not guessed boot crate names; a static no-counter gate must pass before any board run; source/toolchain/workload and root-only exporter remain exact b292
effect: Exact b292 generate build succeeded with fdt_raw/log/ax_alloc excluded symmetrically; 213/233 target compile invocations remained profiled, ELF had 34723 records and 1683280 counter bytes. The calibrated static checker found zero counter writes in named someboot/ax_cpu early functions. Board run1 progressed past early console to Memory Map: then produced no more output for 300s; no shell, counters, profile or full20; session released. Existing ELF shows print_memory_map calls instrumented byte_unit::Byte::get_appropriate_unit whose body contains counter ldxr/stxr, consistent with but not proving the silent stop.
decision: Reject this broad training image; named-function counter-free gate was insufficient because an out-of-line early callee remained instrumented. Avoid another blind broad exclusion iteration; evaluate a narrower exact-source PGO scope around wakeup-relevant runtime crates.
